title: Restriction of the derived coefficient mate equals the projection morphism
statement:
Let $f:Z\to W$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $L_T=-\otimes_A^LB:D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ for ordinary derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $U_T$ for exact restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], for $T=Z,W$. Write $f_A^{-1}\dashv Rf_{*,A}$ and $f_B^{-1}\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ for the canonical adjunctions of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and $\varepsilon_{f,A}$ for the first counit. Use the canonical tensor/pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to identify $f_B^{-1}L_W$ with $L_Zf_A^{-1}$.

Let $J\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and assume $L_ZJ\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and $M=L_W(Rf_{*,A}J)\in D^+(W_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. Define the $B$-linear map $\beta_J:M\to Rf_{*,B}L_ZJ$ to be the adjoint transpose under $f_B^{-1}\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ of
$$f_B^{-1}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Z(f_A^{-1}Rf_{*,A}J)\xrightarrow{L_Z(\varepsilon_{f,A,J})}L_ZJ.$$
Under the canonical identifications $U_TL_TC\cong C\otimes_A^LB_T$ and $U_WRf_{*,B}N\cong Rf_{*,A}U_ZN$, the latter for bounded-below $N$ [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons], the morphism $U_W(\beta_J)$ is exactly
$$\mathrm{PF}_f(J,B_W[0]):(Rf_{*,A}J)\otimes_A^LB_W\longrightarrow Rf_{*,A}(J\otimes_A^LB_Z),$$
the canonical projection-formula morphism of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], where $f_A^{-1}B_W=B_Z$. This is an equality of the specified morphisms, natural in $J$ on the stated bounded-below domain; it asserts no properness, torsion, flatness or invertibility hypothesis and no isomorphism conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0GL6, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings: the identification of scalar change with the projection formula, before the proper/open composition. The normalized map is the counit transpose of def-kun-projection-formula-map, using both identities of lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-derived-adjunction-identities.

proof.text: Put $F_A=f_A^{-1}$, $F_B=f_B^{-1}$, $R_A=Rf_{*,A}$, $R_B=Rf_{*,B}$ and $C=R_AJ$, $N=L_ZJ$, so $M=L_WC$. Write $e_{T,H}:U_TL_TH\simeq H\otimes_A^LB_T$ for the scalar/tensor identification. It is natural on morphisms: $e_{T,H'}\,U_TL_T(v)=(v\otimes1)e_{T,H}$. Indeed [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-comparison] gives this identity on sheaves (with the tensor symmetry to put $B_T$ on the right). Apply it termwise to K-flat resolutions, which exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and compute scalar extension by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Thus it gives precisely the canonical derived identification in the statement, including its action on morphisms. Let $a_H:F_AU_WH\xrightarrow{\sim}U_ZF_BH$ and $d_Q:U_WR_BQ\xrightarrow{\sim}R_AU_ZQ$ be the canonical comparisons of [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons], with these orientations. All uses of these comparisons below are on bounded-below objects: $M,N$ are bounded below by hypothesis, and the right derived images and exact inverse images of bounded-below objects are bounded below.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), and 07A7 (remark-base-change); explicit counit calculation for the coefficient comparison mentioned in more-etale.tex, Tag 0GL6

proof.text:
Let $c_C:F_BL_WC\xrightarrow{\sim}L_ZF_AC$ be the canonical scalar/pullback comparison specified in the statement, and let $t_C:F_A(C\otimes_A^LB_W)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_AC\otimes_A^LB_Z$ be the inverse monoidal comparison used in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Under $e$, forgetting $c_C$ has exactly this normalization:
$$e_{Z,F_AC}\,U_Z(c_C)\,a_{L_WC}=t_C\,F_A(e_{W,C}).$$
To check it, take a K-flat resolution $P$ with flat terms of a complex representing $C$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $F_AP$ remains K-flat with flat terms, and the derived tensor/pullback comparisons are the canonical comparisons on these models. Scalar extension is represented by $P\otimes_AB_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; inverse image is termwise exact as specified in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. After forgetting coefficients both sides are the same ordinary comparison $F_A(P\otimes_AB_W)\to F_AP\otimes_AB_Z$: the scalar/tensor identifications simply retain the tensor and its maps, with the fixed symmetry of step 1. This is a check of the two specified representatives, not an additional projection formula or an isomorphism assertion about direct image.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), and 07A7 (remark-base-change); explicit counit calculation for the coefficient comparison mentioned in more-etale.tex, Tag 0GL6

proof.text:
Put $b=d_N\,U_W(\beta_J):U_WM\to R_AU_ZN$. The counit clause of [lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-derived-adjunction-identities], composed on the right with $F_A(d_N)$, reads
$$\varepsilon^A_{U_ZN}F_A(d_N)=U_Z(\varepsilon^B_N)a_{R_BN}.$$
Consequently the $A$-adjoint transpose of $b$ is
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^A_{U_ZN}F_A(b)
&=U_Z(\varepsilon^B_N)a_{R_BN}F_AU_W(\beta_J)\\
&=U_Z(\varepsilon^B_N)U_ZF_B(\beta_J)a_M\\
&=U_Z\bigl(L_Z(\varepsilon^A_J)c_C\bigr)a_M.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is naturality of $a$ [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]; the third is the defining transpose equation for $\beta_J$ under the canonical adjunction of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The counit identity applies with the bounded-below $B$-object $N$, and naturality applies to the morphism $\beta_J$ between bounded-below $B$-objects $M$ and $R_BN$. Hence no comparison outside the domain of those cited nodes has been used. The counits $\varepsilon^A,\varepsilon^B$ of the cited identity are those of the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction of [sbc-def-base-change-map], which is the canonical derived adjunction of the termwise inverse image and $Ru_*K=Q(u_*I)$ on K-injective resolutions, restricted to $D^+$; [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] fixes this same canonical adjunction for the same functors on the unbounded module derived categories, and [def-kun-projection-formula-map] uses it. So on the bounded-below objects $U_ZN$, $N$ occurring here they are the counits of the adjunctions specified in the statement.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), and 07A7 (remark-base-change); explicit counit calculation for the coefficient comparison mentioned in more-etale.tex, Tag 0GL6

proof.text:
Conjugate $b$ by $e_{W,C}$ on its source and $R_A(e_{Z,J})$ on its target. Naturality of the $A$-counit and step 3 say its transpose is
$$e_{Z,J}U_ZL_Z(\varepsilon^A_J)U_Z(c_C)a_MF_A(e_{W,C}^{-1})
=(\varepsilon^A_J\otimes1_{B_Z})t_C,$$
where the equality uses the naturality of $e$ from step 1 and the normalization from step 2. This is exactly the transpose defining $\mathrm{PF}_f(J,B_W[0])$ in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so the two original morphisms agree. Naturality is also on the stated domain: for $v:J\to J'$ the naturality square for $\varepsilon^A$ gives $v\varepsilon^A_J=\varepsilon^A_{J'}F_AR_A(v)$; applying $L_Z$, naturality of $c$ and the Hom bijection give $R_BL_Z(v)\beta_J=\beta_{J'}L_WR_A(v)$. The natural comparisons $d,e$ carry this square to the projection-morphism square. Only its endpoints must satisfy the hypotheses; no claim that arbitrary scalar extension preserves boundedness is needed.
